summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with token usage, and production systems commonly reduce spend by 50-80% without sacrificing output quality by combining prompt caching, semantic caching, and smart model routing. Prompt caching alone can cut input costs by up to 90% on repeated context, while techniques like model cascading and prompt compression compound those savings. Optimization also improves latency, enabling teams to scale AI usage without proportional cost growth.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse previously processed static portions of a prompt (system instructions, few-shot examples, long documents) so the provider charges a reduced rate for cached input tokens instead of reprocessing them each call.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens (typically 50-90% of input bill on repeated context)
techniques.example: Place a long, unchanging system prompt and document context at the start of every request so Anthropic's prompt caching (cache_control) or OpenAI's automatic caching bills those tokens at a fraction of the normal rate.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store past query-response pairs and return a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (vector similarity) rather than calling the LLM again, avoiding token costs entirely on cache hits.
techniques.savings: 60-70% cost reduction at typical hit rates (~68% hit rates reported)
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming questions and, if cosine similarity to a stored question exceeds 0.95, return the saved answer with zero LLM calls.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, escalating to a larger model only when a small model's confidence or validation fails.
techniques.example: Send simple classification queries to GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku first and only fall back to GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet when the response fails a schema or confidence check.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduce the number of input tokens by removing redundancy, shortening instructions, and compressing context using tools like LLMLingua while preserving task-critical information.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved documents through Microsoft's LLMLingua to compress them 3-5x before injecting them into a RAG prompt, cutting input tokens with minimal accuracy loss.

techniques.name: Output Token Control (max_tokens & concise prompts)
techniques.description: Cap response length and instruct the model to be concise, since output tokens are often 2-4x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens to a tight bound and add 'Respond in under 50 words, no preamble' to stop the model from generating verbose, costly explanations.

techniques.name: Structured Output / Function Calling
techniques.description: Request compact structured responses (JSON, enums) instead of free-form prose to minimize output tokens and eliminate downstream re-prompting for reformatting.
techniques.example: Use OpenAI structured outputs with a JSON schema so the model returns {"sentiment":"positive"} rather than a paragraph explaining its reasoning.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Context Trimming
techniques.description: Retrieve and inject only the top-k most relevant chunks rather than entire documents, and rerank to keep context small.
techniques.savings: 30-70% reduction in input tokens versus full-document stuffing
techniques.example: Retrieve the top 3 reranked passages for a question instead of the full 50-page manual, reducing prompt size from 40k to 2k tokens.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Combine multiple independent tasks into a single API call or use provider batch APIs that offer discounted asynchronous processing.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% via batch API discounts plus reduced overhead
techniques.example: Use OpenAI's Batch API for non-urgent bulk classification jobs to get a 50% discount on both input and output tokens.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Stopping
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed answer or a stop sequence appears, avoiding wasted output tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '</answer>' so generation halts immediately after the structured answer closes instead of rambling further.

techniques.name: Fine-Tuned/Distilled Small Models
techniques.description: Distill a large model's behavior into a smaller, cheaper fine-tuned model for a narrow task, reducing per-token cost and latency at inference.
techniques.savings: 60-90% per-call cost reduction for the targeted task
techniques.example: Fine-tune GPT-4o-mini on 1,000 labeled examples so it matches GPT-4o quality on your extraction task at a fraction of the cost.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores LLM responses and serves cached results for semantically similar queries using vector similarity.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (self-hosted; infra costs only)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK to call 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, support, and managed features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, caching, cost analytics, and prompt management.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo (Pro) scaling with usage

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used to implement low-latency semantic caching of LLM prompts and responses.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Redis Cloud free tier then usage-based from ~$5/mo; Enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (InMemory, Redis, SQLite, GPTCache), prompt templating, and model routing abstractions.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt compression toolkit that compresses prompts up to 20x to cut input tokens while preserving task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, load balancing, automatic fallbacks, and observability across multiple providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$49/mo

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API that routes requests across many providers/models with transparent pricing, enabling cheap-model fallback and cost comparison.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go with a small routing fee on credits; no subscription required

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching for static system prompts and long context (up to 90% off cached input tokens) with minimal code changes.
Set tight max_tokens limits and add 'be concise, no preamble' to prompts to slash expensive output tokens.
Route easy requests to a cheaper model (GPT-4o-mini / Claude Haiku) and only escalate on failure for 50-80% blended savings.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to serve ~68% of repeat/similar queries with zero LLM calls.
Move non-urgent bulk workloads to provider Batch APIs for an immediate ~50% discount on tokens.
